headline: Week 1: snap counts separate the booms from the busts
overview: The model's Week 1 board is built almost entirely on role, not reputation. Seven of the eight boom calls come with a rising three-game snap share or touch count, while six of the eight busts are players whose usage has quietly collapsed. Two matchups do most of the heavy lifting: Cincinnati's defense against Tampa Bay's backfield, and Dallas's secondary against the Giants.

sections.title: Games the projections lean into
sections.body: Tampa Bay at Cincinnati is the model's favorite environment, with the Bengals carrying the 29th-ranked defense in the game list and giving up the most RB scoring in the league at 28.3 PPR/game. Dallas at New York is the other one: the Cowboys' defense ranks 32nd here and allows 39.3 PPR/game to receivers. San Francisco at Los Angeles adds a third, with the 49ers' 24th-ranked defense facing the second-best offense on the slate.

sections.title: Snap share is doing the talking
sections.body: Every boom call except Nabers comes with a rising role. Malik Willis is up 31 points of snap share, RJ Harvey up 18, Ashton Jeanty up 12 and Kenny Gainwell up 13 over their last three games. On the other side, Jordan Love is down 58 points, Jaylen Waddle down 30 and Josh Jacobs down 26, and none of those three faces a defense that forgives a reduced role.

sections.title: Regression watch
sections.body: Derrick Henry at 27.0 PPR/game over the last 3 against a 16.4 season average is the kind of run that usually cools off, and Indianapolis has held backs to 19.9 PPR/game. The model still likes him because the touches are real at 25.0 a game and the Colts allow 28.8 points/game. The tight ends go the other way: Dalton Kincaid and Jake Ferguson have both seen their target share cut roughly in half and both draw defenses inside the league's top dozen against the position.

sections.title: Under the radar
sections.body: Gainwell is the name to chase. He is listed second behind Bucky Irving, yet his snap share has climbed to 63% and his touches to 13.7 a game, and the matchup grades a perfect 10.0/10 for running backs. Harvey is the same idea in a harder spot, with a 44% carry share and Dobbins not expected to play.
